examples.source: If your account has multiple instances that can access the requested QPU
examples.translation: Kung ang iyong account ay mayroon maraming instance na maaaring ma-access ang hiniling na QPU
examples.suggested: Kung may maraming instance ang iyong account na may access sa hiniling na QPU
examples.why: 'mayroon maraming' is missing the linker (it should be 'mayroong'). 'instance na maaaring ma-access ang QPU' also reverses the agent, so it reads as though the instance is what gets accessed.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide
examples.translation: Sundin ang mga hakbang sa [Hello world](/guides/hello-world)
examples.suggested: Sundin ang mga hakbang sa gabay na [Patakbuhin ang iyong unang circuit sa hardware](/guides/hello-world)
examples.why: The link label was replaced with an old page title, and the word 'guide' was dropped. It is harmless, but it no longer matches the source.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a few things need a native editor's touch. "From source" is translated as "mula sa pinagmulan" (entries 1, 3, 4, 30). That reads as "from the origin" and loses the meaning of building from the source code. "Mula sa source code" would be clearer. "Environment" appears both as "virtual environment" (entry 5) and as "kapaligiran" (entries 6, 12). "Kapaligiran" is the everyday word for surroundings, not a Python environment. Entries 22 and 28 use the calque "polusyon ng iyong global na Python installation". Entry 4 also drops the "therefore" that links its two sentences.

examples.source: When you install `qiskit-ibm-runtime` from source, you can access the current development version
examples.translation: Kapag nag-install ka ng `qiskit-ibm-runtime` mula sa pinagmulan, maaari kang mag-access ng kasalukuyang development version
examples.suggested: Kapag in-install mo ang `qiskit-ibm-runtime` mula sa source code, maa-access mo ang kasalukuyang development version
examples.why: 'Pinagmulan' means origin or provenance, not source code, so a learner loses the point of building from the repository's code. The same rendering appears in entries 1, 3 and 30.

examples.source: create a minimal environment with only Python installed in it
examples.translation: lumikha ng minimal na kapaligiran na may Python lamang na naka-install dito
examples.suggested: gumawa ng minimal na environment na Python lang ang naka-install
examples.why: The heading in entry 5 keeps 'virtual environment' in English, but entries 6 and 12 switch to 'kapaligiran'. That is the everyday word for surroundings, so the same concept gets two names in one file.

examples.source: to avoid polluting your global Python installation
examples.translation: para maiwasan ang polusyon ng iyong global na Python installation
examples.suggested: para hindi magulo o madumihan ang global na Python installation mo
examples.why: 'Polusyon' is a literal calque of the English metaphor and sounds odd in a software context. Entry 28 repeats it.

examples.source: You can therefore inspect and extend the latest version of the code more efficiently.
examples.translation: Maaari kang mag-inspect at mag-extend ng pinakabagong bersyon ng code nang mas mahusay.
examples.suggested: Kaya mas madali mong masusuri at mapapalawak ang pinakabagong bersyon ng code.
examples.why: 'Therefore' is dropped, so the cause-and-effect link between installing from source and working more efficiently is lost. 'Mag-inspect/mag-extend' also reads as stiff Taglish.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and the terms (quantum circuit, gate, measurement, transpilation, lingua franca) are handled consistently in a casual register with no po/opo. In the quoted paper passage [6], "given the hardware constraints" is rendered as "dahil sa mga hardware constraint" ("because of"). That makes the constraints sound like the reason a language is practical to compile, when the source means "while working within" them. "Isinasaalang-alang ang" or "sa kabila ng" would fit better. There are also a few calques, such as "mga ordered na sequence" in [3], and in [4] the link text now contains a comma that belongs outside it ("[OpenQASM 3,]").

examples.source: prefer languages that are practical to compile given the hardware constraints
examples.translation: mas gusto ang mga language na praktikal para i-compile dahil sa mga hardware constraint
examples.suggested: mas gusto ang mga language na praktikal i-compile kung isasaalang-alang ang mga hardware constraint
examples.why: 'dahil sa' means 'because of' and changes the logic slightly. The source means 'considering' or 'within' the constraints.

examples.source: as ordered sequences of parameterized operations
examples.translation: bilang mga ordered na sequence ng parameterized na operasyon
examples.suggested: bilang mga nakaayos na sunod-sunod na parameterized na operasyon
examples.why: 'ordered na sequence' is a word-for-word calque. A Tagalog technical writer would put the ordering idea into Tagalog.

examples.source: the latest version, [OpenQASM 3](...), incorporates
examples.translation: ang pinakabagong bersyon, [OpenQASM 3,](...) ay nagsasama
examples.suggested: ang pinakabagong bersyon, [OpenQASM 3](...), ay nagsasama
examples.why: The comma has moved inside the link text. It is a small markup slip that should be put back outside the link.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The Hinton colors (white is positive, black is negative), the Bloch caveat that the plot cannot show entanglement correlations, and the qsphere-only figsize exception all come through correctly. The problems are in the verb forms. 'Plot' is conjugated as the nonstandard 'nipo-plot' in [14], [19], [23], [33] and [36], where 'pina-plot'/'ipina-plot' would be normal. 'Ipinaprojekt' in [36] and 'ipinagpapalagay' in [6] are also malformed. In [27], 'ay lahat ng observable' reads as 'are all the observables that return ±1', which is slightly stronger than the English; 'ay pawang mga observable' would fix that.

examples.source: how Qiskit's different visualization functions plot the following quantum state
examples.translation: kung paano nipo-plot ng iba't ibang visualization function ng Qiskit
examples.suggested: kung paano ipina-plot ng iba't ibang visualization function ng Qiskit
examples.why: 'nipo-plot' is not a standard Tagalog conjugation of i-plot. The same form repeats in [19], [23], [33] and [36].

examples.source: This plot projects multi-qubit quantum states onto the single-qubit space
examples.translation: Ipinaprojekt ng plot na ito ang mga multi-qubit quantum state
examples.suggested: Ipina-project ng plot na ito ang mga multi-qubit quantum state
examples.why: This is a malformed hybrid spelling. The normal convention for English loan verbs is a hyphenated affix.

examples.source: Here we assume you already have a particular state
examples.translation: Dito ipinagpapalagay namin na mayroon ka nang partikular na estado
examples.suggested: Dito, ipinapalagay namin na mayroon ka nang partikular na estado
examples.why: 'ipinagpapalagay' is a nonstandard form of the verb; 'ipinapalagay' is the correct one.

examples.source: Tensor products of Pauli matrices are all observables that return +1 or -1.
examples.translation: Ang mga tensor product ng Pauli matrix ay lahat ng observable na nagbabalik ng +1 o -1.
examples.suggested: Ang mga tensor product ng Pauli matrix ay pawang mga observable na nagbabalik ng +1 o -1.
examples.why: 'ay lahat ng observable' can be read as 'are all the observables that return ±1', which is slightly stronger than the English. 'pawang' removes that reading.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall: the benchmark caveats, the REM-vs-unmitigated distinction in [51]/[68] and the complementary-scale note in [69] all come through intact. Entry [31] renders "roughly scales as" with "sumusukat" ("measures"), which garbles the scaling claim but leaves the formula readable. Two smaller slips: [15] turns the sequential "then" into "rin" ("also"), and [25] changes "similar structural properties" into "magkaparehong istruktura" ("identical structure"). "Precision" is split between "katumpakan" ([22]), which also stands for accuracy, and English "precision" ([33], [38]). A few phrasings are stiff: [38] "malaki ang pagiging hindi ganoon katumpak", [39] "magiging haba na 1", [73] "kaalamang" (should be "maalam na").

examples.source: This method has a QPU time overhead that roughly scales as:
examples.translation: Ang method na ito ay may QPU time overhead na humigit-kumulang na sumusukat gaya ng:
examples.suggested: Ang method na ito ay may QPU time overhead na humigit-kumulang lumalaki (nag-i-scale) ayon sa:
examples.why: 'Sumusukat' means 'measures', not 'scales'. The sentence is introducing a scaling law.

examples.source: QESEM then runs a set of characterization-based ES and EM circuits on the QPU
examples.translation: Nagpapatakbo rin ang QESEM ng isang hanay ng mga characterization-based na ES at EM circuit
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, nagpapatakbo ang QESEM ng isang hanay ng mga characterization-based na ES at EM circuit
examples.why: 'Rin' (also) drops the order of steps, which the English sets out explicitly (first transpile, then run).

examples.source: results of the same quality will be obtained for different circuits with similar structural properties
examples.translation: makukuha ang parehong kalidad ng mga resulta para sa iba't ibang circuit na may magkaparehong istruktura
examples.suggested: makukuha ang parehong kalidad ng mga resulta para sa iba't ibang circuit na may magkakahawig na katangiang pang-istruktura
examples.why: 'Magkaparehong' means identical, not similar, so the translation narrows the claim.

examples.source: '$\epsilon$' is the absolute precision of the mitigation
examples.translation: ang '$\epsilon$' ay ang absolute na katumpakan ng mitigation
examples.suggested: ang '$\epsilon$' ay ang absolute precision ng mitigation
examples.why: 'Katumpakan' is used for 'accuracy' throughout the file. Using it here as well blurs precision and accuracy in the very sentence that defines accuracy in terms of epsilon. Later entries keep 'precision' in English.

examples.source: they are significantly less accurate than the final results
examples.translation: malaki ang pagiging hindi ganoon katumpak nito kumpara sa mga panghuling resulta
examples.suggested: mas hindi hamak na tumpak ang mga ito kumpara sa mga panghuling resulta
examples.why: The phrasing is stiff and circuitous, and the wording is calqued from English.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The QPY compatibility caveat in [6] ("bagaman hindi tiyak na compatible sa mas lumang mga bersyon") is kept, and so is the note in [9] that qpy.load always returns a list. The one slip is in [9]: "i-re-load" stacks two English prefixes into a stiff hybrid, and a native technical writer would write "i-load muli".

examples.source: you can re-load the circuit using the `qpy.load` function
examples.translation: maaari mong i-re-load ang circuit gamit ang `qpy.load` function
examples.suggested: maaari mong i-load muli ang circuit gamit ang `qpy.load` function
examples.why: 'i-re-load' is an awkward double-prefixed calque. The Tagalog 'muli' says 're-' more naturally.

editor_note: In [6], "can run over many sessions" is rendered "maaaring tumaas sa maraming session". "Tumaas" means "rise/increase", so the sentence comes out garbled rather than saying that workflows span several sessions. It should be "maaaring umabot/tumagal nang maraming session". In [8], "maaari kang tingnan" is ungrammatical and should be "maaari mong tingnan". In [14], "then" becomes "ring" ("also"), which loses the save-then-load order. None of these would give a learner a false technical belief. Terms are consistent throughout: job, i-retrieve, i-save, kernel and backend.

examples.source: can run over many sessions
examples.translation: maaaring tumaas sa maraming session
examples.suggested: maaaring umabot nang maraming session
examples.why: 'tumaas' means 'increase/rise'. The workflow isn't growing, it spans several sessions, so the sentence is confusing as written.

examples.source: or you can see all your submitted jobs
examples.translation: o maaari kang tingnan ang lahat ng iyong mga na-submit na job
examples.suggested: o maaari mong tingnan ang lahat ng iyong na-submit na job
examples.why: This verb takes the object-focus form, so the actor pronoun has to be 'mong', not 'kang'.

examples.source: You can then load this array from disk in a separate kernel.
examples.translation: Maaari mo ring i-load ang array na ito mula sa disk sa isang hiwalay na kernel.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, maaari mong i-load ang array na ito mula sa disk sa isang hiwalay na kernel.
examples.why: 'ring' (also) replaces 'then', so the order of saving first and loading later is lost.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. Conditions, negations and caveats all survive: the undefined `--qpu` resource "hindi papansinin" [14], the `{}` environment case [15], the Open Plan batch-mode fallback [17], the no-restart note [29], and the env settings applying "lamang" to `--qpu` jobs [38]. Two things a native editor would still change. In [20], "ang `CMakeLists.txt` na file ay inaasahang ang ... ay matatagpuan" copies the English sentence structure and reads stiffly. In [17], "workaround" becomes "solusyon", which loses the sense that batch mode is only a stopgap.

examples.source: By default, the `CMakeLists.txt` file expects the Slurm header file (`slurm.h`) to be located in `/usr/include/slurm`
examples.translation: Sa default, ang `CMakeLists.txt` na file ay inaasahang ang Slurm header file (`slurm.h`) ay matatagpuan sa `/usr/include/slurm`
examples.suggested: Bilang default, inaasahan ng `CMakeLists.txt` na nasa `/usr/include/slurm` ang Slurm header file (`slurm.h`)
examples.why: The double 'ay' copies the English sentence structure. 'Sa default' is also a calque, and 'inaasahang' has the wrong linker form here.

examples.source: add `QRMI_IBM_QRS_SESSION_MODE="batch"` ... as aworkaround.
examples.translation: ... bilang solusyon.
examples.suggested: ... bilang pansamantalang solusyon (workaround).
examples.why: 'Solusyon' presents batch mode as a full fix. It is a workaround for accounts without session support, and that nuance is softened.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The support routing, the Trial-account caveats ("malamang mawawala ang iyong access") and the billing and verification conditions in the admonition all match the English, and nothing in the page would mislead a learner. There are three small slips. Entry [8] renders "job errors" as "mga error sa trabaho", which reads as errors at one's workplace rather than errors in a submitted quantum job. Entry [0] has the typo "narararanasan", which should be "nararanasan". Entry [7] uses "case" and then "kaso" for the same thing within a single sentence.

examples.source: including platform issues, job errors, Qiskit guidance
examples.translation: kasama na ang mga isyu sa platform, mga error sa trabaho, gabay sa Qiskit
examples.suggested: kasama na ang mga isyu sa platform, mga error sa job, gabay sa Qiskit
examples.why: 'Trabaho' means work or employment. In Qiskit, a 'job' is a submitted workload, and the field keeps that term in English.

examples.source: questions or problems you encounter
examples.translation: mga tanong o problema na narararanasan mo
examples.suggested: mga tanong o problema na nararanasan mo
examples.why: Typo: the reduplication is wrong. The correct form is 'nararanasan'.

examples.source: To see all your open IBM Cloud cases or to open a new case
examples.translation: lahat ng iyong bukas na IBM Cloud case o para magbukas ng bagong kaso
examples.suggested: lahat ng iyong bukas na IBM Cloud case o para magbukas ng bagong case
examples.why: The same term is rendered two ways in one sentence. Elsewhere the page uses 'kaso' ([15]) or keeps 'Cloud Case' ([6]), so pick one form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The cost caveats are kept exactly: the "Hindi ka sisingilin maliban kung..." note in [19], the "may kasamang bayad" underline in [21] and the Open or free plan exception. The casual register holds, with no po/opo. There are two small fixes. In [3], "work with users" (meaning administer users on the instance) is rendered "pakikipagtulungan sa mga user", which suggests collaborating with users. In [15], "Pagkatapos mo mag-upgrade" is missing the linker and should be "Pagkatapos mong mag-upgrade".

examples.source: set up a service instance, and work with users
examples.translation: pag-set up ng service instance, at pakikipagtulungan sa mga user
examples.suggested: pag-set up ng service instance, at pamamahala ng mga user
examples.why: "Pakikipagtulungan" means collaborating. In this admin guide, "work with users" means managing the users on an instance.

examples.source: After you upgrade, you can continue to use any instances
examples.translation: Pagkatapos mo mag-upgrade, maaari mo pa ring gamitin
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos mong mag-upgrade, maaari mo pa ring gamitin
examples.why: The linker -ng is missing between the pronoun and the verb, so the phrase reads as a small grammar slip.

editor_note: Nothing in the translation would mislead a learner, and the key limit is kept: VPEs work only for the API and SDK, and the website works only over the public network. In [5], "Regardless of whether you use VPEs" became the vague "Anuman ang gamitin mo" ("whatever you use"). That drops the mention of VPEs, so the reader loses the link to the next paragraph. There are also a few stiff calques. "scales horizontally" → "nagpapalaki nang pahalang" in [4] and the sentence-final "sa halip" in [6] both read awkwardly. In [24], "ay maaaring ma-access ang" mixes up the grammar: the passive ma-access doesn't fit a sentence where the server instances do the accessing.

examples.source: Regardless of whether you use VPEs, all internal communication ... always uses private connections
examples.translation: Anuman ang gamitin mo, gumagamit palagi ang lahat ng internal na komunikasyon ...
examples.suggested: Gumamit ka man ng VPE o hindi, palaging gumagamit ng mga private na koneksyon ang lahat ng internal na komunikasyon ...
examples.why: The mention of VPEs is dropped, so 'whatever you use' has no clear referent and the contrast set up for the next paragraph is lost.

examples.source: Now your virtual server instances in the VPC can access your IBM Quantum Platform instance privately.
examples.translation: Ngayon ang iyong mga virtual server instance sa VPC ay maaaring ma-access ang iyong IBM Quantum Platform instance nang pribado.
examples.suggested: Ngayon, makaka-access na nang pribado ang iyong mga virtual server instance sa VPC sa iyong IBM Quantum Platform instance.
examples.why: The passive 'ma-access' doesn't match the active subject and 'ang' object, which makes the sentence ungrammatical.

examples.source: a virtualized function that scales horizontally
examples.translation: isang virtualized na function na nagpapalaki nang pahalang
examples.suggested: isang virtualized na function na nag-i-scale nang pahorizontal (horizontal scaling)
examples.why: 'nagpapalaki nang pahalang' is a literal calque; the field keeps the term 'horizontal scaling' in English.

examples.source: Connecting through a VPE keeps that traffic on the private network instead.
examples.translation: Ang pagkonekta sa pamamagitan ng VPE ay pinapanatili ang trapikong iyon sa private network sa halip.
examples.suggested: Sa halip, pinapanatili ng pagkonekta sa pamamagitan ng VPE ang trapikong iyon sa private network.
examples.why: Putting 'sa halip' at the end copies English word order, and 'ay pinapanatili ang' reads stiffly.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. It does have three small slips a native editor would fix. In [21], "kung saan ito nag-save" uses the completed aspect ("where it saved"), but the English means where it will save, so "kung saan nito ise-save" is better. In [25], "for brevity" became "para sa kaginhawahan" ("for convenience"), a mild word shift. In [33], "nagscale" is a malformed verb and should be "nag-i-scale" or "nagsi-scale".

examples.source: the `filename` kwarg takes a path to which it saves the rendered output
examples.translation: ang `filename` kwarg ay tumatanggap ng path kung saan ito nag-save ng rendered output
examples.suggested: ang `filename` kwarg ay tumatanggap ng path kung saan nito ise-save ang rendered output
examples.why: The completed aspect 'nag-save' implies a past action. The English describes where the output will be saved.

examples.source: `mpl` is used here for brevity.
examples.translation: ginagamit dito ang `mpl` para sa kaginhawahan.
examples.suggested: ginagamit dito ang `mpl` para maikli.
examples.why: 'Kaginhawahan' means convenience, not brevity. The reason given shifts slightly, but it is harmless.

examples.source: The `scale` option scales the output of the `mpl` and `latex` renderers.
examples.translation: Ang `scale` na opsyon ay nagscale ng output ng `mpl` at `latex` renderer.
examples.suggested: Ang `scale` na opsyon ay nag-i-scale ng output ng `mpl` at `latex` renderer.
examples.why: 'nagscale' is a malformed Taglish verb. It needs a hyphen and reduplication to be correct.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The plot_histogram options (asc/desc, number_to_keep "rest", bar_labels) and the Estimator error-bar passage all match the source. A few small wording fixes would help. "Expectation values" in [24] comes out as the half-calque "mga halaga ng expectation", where "mga expectation value" is the usual form. Calling a function is "tawagin" in [9] but "Tawagan" in [10]. The phrase "hayagan na ipakita" in [9] and the literal "Ang `savefig()` na paraan" for "method" in [10] both read stiffly.

examples.source: estimates the expectation values of seven different observables
examples.translation: tinatantya ng sumusunod na cell ang mga halaga ng expectation ng pitong iba't ibang observable
examples.suggested: tinatantya ng sumusunod na cell ang mga expectation value ng pitong magkakaibang observable
examples.why: 'Expectation value' is a fixed term in the field. Breaking it into 'halaga ng expectation' is a half-calque that makes the term harder to recognize.

examples.source: Call `.show()` on the returned object
examples.translation: Tawagan ang `.show()` sa ibinalik na object
examples.suggested: Tawagin ang `.show()` sa ibinalik na object
examples.why: Entry [9] uses 'tawagin' for calling a function. 'Tawagan' sounds like making a phone call, and it makes the file inconsistent.

examples.source: you will need to explicitly show or save the outputs
examples.translation: kailangan mong hayagan na ipakita o i-save ang mga output
examples.suggested: kailangan mong tahasang ipakita o i-save ang mga output
examples.why: 'Hayagan na' is a stiff rendering of 'explicitly'. 'Tahasang' is the more natural adverb here.

editor_note: The translation is faithful on the main points: the classical-control logic, the four outcome cases, the no-cloning argument and "burning" the e-bit all come through correctly. "Communicate" (qubits) is translated as "ipahayag/maipahayag" in [83] and [84]. That word means "express/declare", so the key contrast in [84] (using teleportation to apply operations rather than transmit qubits) becomes blurred. It should be "ipadala", which the file uses elsewhere. [23] has a garbled clause, "nasa state man lamang na ang qubit Q", where "man lamang" reads as "at least" rather than "whatever state". [37] drops the "nor less" half of "neither more nor less associated". There are also small grammar slips: "maaari tayong subukan muli", "pinakakaliwa qubit" (missing the -ng linker) and the doubled "nagpapadala ang isang nagpapadala" in [2].

examples.source: uses teleportation to apply *operations* to qubits rather than communicating them
examples.translation: gumagamit ng teleportation para mag-apply ng mga *operasyon* sa mga qubit sa halip na ipahayag ang mga ito
examples.suggested: ... sa halip na ipadala ang mga ito
examples.why: 'ipahayag' means express/declare, not transmit, so the operations-vs-transmission contrast that defines gate teleportation is lost. The same misrendering appears in [83] ('sana'y maipahayag natin').

examples.source: the qubit B will be in whatever state Q was in prior to the protocol being executed
examples.translation: ang qubit $\mathsf{B}$ ay nasa state man lamang na ang qubit $\mathsf{Q}$ noong bago pa isagawa ang protocol
examples.suggested: ang qubit $\mathsf{B}$ ay mapupunta sa kung anumang state na kinaroroonan ng $\mathsf{Q}$ bago isagawa ang protocol
examples.why: The clause is ungrammatical, and 'man lamang' ('at least') does not mean 'whatever state'. This is the central claim of the protocol, so it should read cleanly.

examples.source: α and β are neither more nor less associated with the leftmost qubit than they are with the other qubits
examples.translation: ang $\alpha$ at $\beta$ ay hindi mas nakakonekta sa pinakakaliwa qubit kaysa sa ibang mga qubit
examples.suggested: ang $\alpha$ at $\beta$ ay hindi mas o mas kaunting nakaugnay sa pinakakaliwang qubit kaysa sa ibang mga qubit
examples.why: This drops 'nor less', which weakens the symmetric point. It also misses the -ng linker ('pinakakaliwang'), and 'lumilipad nang malaya' in the same entry is a calque of 'float freely'.

examples.source: if the process doesn't work out, we can just try again
examples.translation: maaari tayong subukan muli
examples.suggested: maaari lang nating subukan ulit
examples.why: 'tayong subukan' makes 'we' the thing being tried. The actor form needs 'nating'.

editor_note: Two sentences mislead the learner. In [22], "we would not get far in understanding quantum information without them" became "hindi tayo malayo sa pag-unawa ... nang wala ang mga ito", which reads as "we are not far from understanding it without them" and reverses the point of the sentence. In [110], "second-to-last equality" became "pangalawa hanggang huling pagkakapantay-pantay" ("second through last equality"), which points to the wrong step of the derivation. There are also minor slips: [85] is broken ("Dahil ang anumang orthonormal set…" means "because any…" where the source says "given any…"), and it leaves "Pictorially" in English. "Express" is rendered as "isinasalita" ("to speak") in [9] and [28], and [66] and [111] use calques ("nabubuhay", "Teknikalisyong nagsasalita").

examples.source: we would not get far in understanding quantum information at a mathematical level without them.
examples.translation: hindi tayo malayo sa pag-unawa ng quantum information sa antas ng matematika nang wala ang mga ito.
examples.suggested: hindi tayo makakarating nang malayo sa pag-unawa ng quantum information sa antas ng matematika kung wala ang mga ito.
examples.why: 'hindi tayo malayo' means 'we are not far (from it)', which suggests we are close to understanding without inner products. That is the opposite of the source.

examples.source: implies the second-to-last equality
examples.translation: ay nagpapahiwatig ng pangalawa hanggang huling pagkakapantay-pantay
examples.suggested: ang dahilan ng ikalawa-mula-sa-huling pagkakapantay-pantay
examples.why: 'pangalawa hanggang huli' reads as 'the second through the last' equalities, so it points to the wrong step of the derivation.

examples.source: Given any orthonormal set of vectors ... there exists a unitary matrix U ... Pictorially, we can always find
examples.translation: Dahil ang anumang orthonormal set ng mga vector ... may isang unitary matrix ... Pictorially, palagi tayong makakahanap
examples.suggested: Para sa anumang orthonormal set ng mga vector ... may unitary matrix ... Kung ilalarawan sa larawan, palagi tayong makakahanap
examples.why: 'Dahil' ('because') makes the sentence ungrammatical, and 'Pictorially' is left untranslated.

examples.source: we express a column vector as a ket
examples.translation: isinasalita natin ang isang column vector bilang ket
examples.suggested: ipinapahayag natin ang isang column vector bilang ket
examples.why: 'isalita' means to speak aloud. For mathematical expression the word is 'ipahayag', which the file itself uses elsewhere.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the Born rule, the argument that H tells |+⟩ and |−⟩ apart, the square root of NOT, and the permutation-matrix claim all come through correctly. But 'if and only if' is rendered twice as 'kung at kung' ([88], [135]). That drops 'lamang' and loses the 'only if' direction, so it should be 'kung at kung lamang'. A few more slips: 'compact form' as 'maigting na anyo' ('maigting' means tense, not compact); 'sum to 1' as 'nagkakabuod sa 1'; 'as far as … are concerned' as 'sa pagitan ng' ('between'); and calques like 'kahit man sa bahagi', 'hindi natin ginawang abala' and the non-standard 'tinukuyan' for 'defined'.

examples.source: an $n\times n$ matrix $U$ is unitary if and only if
examples.translation: ang isang $n\times n$ matrix na $U$ ay unitary kung at kung
examples.suggested: ang isang $n\times n$ matrix na $U$ ay unitary kung at kung lamang
examples.why: 'kung at kung' means 'if and if'. Without 'lamang' the biconditional is not expressed. The same problem is in [135].

examples.source: supports precise descriptions of large and complicated vectors in a compact form
examples.translation: sa isang maigting na anyo
examples.suggested: sa isang siksik (compact) na anyo
examples.why: 'Maigting' means tense or taut, not concise or compact.

examples.source: as far as standard basis measurements are concerned, the plus and minus states are no different
examples.translation: sa pagitan ng mga standard basis measurement, walang pagkakaiba ang plus at minus state
examples.suggested: pagdating sa mga standard basis measurement, walang pagkakaiba ang plus at minus state
examples.why: 'Sa pagitan ng' means 'between', which garbles the scoping phrase.

examples.source: the absolute values squared of the entries in a quantum state vector sum to $1$
examples.translation: ay nagkakabuod sa $1$
examples.suggested: ay may kabuuang $1$
examples.why: 'Nagkakabuod' is not a natural way to say 'sum to'. The page elsewhere uses 'kabuuan'.

examples.source: we did not bother to convert to the equivalent matrix/vector forms
examples.translation: hindi natin ginawang abala na i-convert
examples.suggested: hindi na tayo nag-abalang i-convert
examples.why: This is a literal calque of 'did not bother'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, but it has a few literal calques. In [9], "fast-track" is rendered as "mabilis na masubaybayan", which means "be quickly tracked/monitored" and misreads the idiom. The overall point still comes through (the resources help and simplify learning), so I don't count it as a fail. In [7], "near-term quantum advantage" becomes "panandaliang quantum advantage", which can read as a temporary advantage. In [13], "purpose, objectives" collapses into the repeated "layunin, mga layunin", and in [54] "branch out" is flattened to "sumulong" ("advance").

examples.source: These resources will help your team fast-track and simplify their quantum computing learning journey.
examples.translation: makakatulong sa iyong koponan na mabilis na masubaybayan at pasimplehin ang kanilang paglalakbay
examples.suggested: makakatulong sa iyong koponan na pabilisin at pasimplehin ang kanilang paglalakbay sa pag-aaral ng quantum computing
examples.why: 'Mabilis na masubaybayan' means 'be quickly monitored/tracked'. It is a literal calque of 'track' and changes what the sentence claims.

examples.source: a focus area that targets near-term quantum advantage
examples.translation: isang focus area na nagta-target ng panandaliang quantum advantage
examples.suggested: isang focus area na nagta-target ng quantum advantage sa malapit na hinaharap
examples.why: 'Panandalian' suggests short-lived or temporary. That makes it sound like the advantage is fleeting, when the English means it is expected soon.

examples.source: defining the current near-term purpose, objectives, and required actions
examples.translation: pagtukoy ng kasalukuyang panandaliang layunin, mga layunin, at mga kinakailangang aksyon
examples.suggested: pagtukoy ng kasalukuyang layunin sa malapit na hinaharap, mga target, at mga kinakailangang aksyon
examples.why: 'Purpose' and 'objectives' both become 'layunin', so the list repeats the same word and loses the distinction between them.

examples.source: Start with your comfort zone(s) and branch out.
examples.translation: Magsimula sa iyong mga comfort zone at sumulong.
examples.suggested: Magsimula sa iyong mga comfort zone at unti-unting lumawak sa ibang larangan.
examples.why: 'Sumulong' means 'move forward', which drops the idea of branching out into adjacent areas.

editor_note: In entry [12] the translation drops "too", which reverses the meaning. "maaaring mataas pa rin upang payagan ang buong circuit na gumana nang tama" literally says the new error rate is still high enough to let the circuit work correctly. The source says it may be too high for the circuit to work, and that is the whole motivation for concatenation. There are also word-choice and calque problems. "motivates" is rendered as "nagmumudmod" in [10], which is the wrong verb (it should be "nag-uudyok"). "translate to" is calqued as "nagsasalin sa" in [6] and [11]. "matagumpay tayong mababawasan" in [10] is ungrammatical, and [12] and [13] have the misspellings "teorytikong" and "inaaalisin".

examples.source: However, this new error rate might still be too high to allow the entire circuit to work correctly.
examples.translation: Gayunpaman, ang bagong error rate na ito ay maaaring mataas pa rin upang payagan ang buong circuit na gumana nang tama.
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, maaaring masyado pa ring mataas ang bagong error rate na ito para gumana nang tama ang buong circuit.
examples.why: Dropping 'too' ('masyado') makes the sentence say the high error rate lets the circuit work. That is the opposite of the intended caveat, which motivates concatenation.

examples.source: This, in fact, motivates less forgiving noise models where errors might not be independent
examples.translation: Ito, sa katotohanan, ay nagmumudmod ng mas hindi nagpapatawad na noise models
examples.suggested: Ito nga ang nag-uudyok na gumamit ng mas mahigpit na noise models
examples.why: 'nagmumudmod' (to dip or rub) is the wrong verb for 'motivates', and 'mas hindi nagpapatawad' is a stiff calque of 'less forgiving'.

examples.source: then we will succeed in reducing the error probability
examples.translation: matagumpay tayong mababawasan ang error probability
examples.suggested: magtatagumpay tayong bawasan ang error probability
examples.why: The verb form is ungrammatical: 'mababawasan' cannot take 'tayo' as the actor this way.

examples.source: this translates to a reduction in error.
examples.translation: ito ay nagsasalin sa pagbabawas ng error.
examples.suggested: nangangahulugan ito ng pagbaba ng error.
examples.why: 'nagsasalin' is a calque of 'translates to' (it means 'translates' only in the linguistic sense). The same calque appears in [6].

examples.source: various technical details we're omitting here.
examples.translation: iba't ibang teknikal na detalye na ating inaaalisin dito.
examples.suggested: iba't ibang teknikal na detalyeng nilalaktawan natin dito.
examples.why: 'inaaalisin' is a misspelling, and 'nilalaktawan' fits 'omitting' better. [12] also has the misspelling 'teorytikong' (should be 'teoretikal').

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The surface-code edge cases, the rotated-code explanation, the three-colouring condition for colour codes and the [[144,12,12]] gross code all match the English. The problems are small surface slips. [8] has an ungrammatical doubled object ("Maaari rin itong i-cut ang mga gilid"). [12] has a typo ("tatalakaying"). [21] uses a non-standard verb form ("nagtatukoy") and the stiff calque "nagngangalang ganito". [17] also drops "therefore" (kaya), so the link between the face structure and geometric locality is weaker than in the English.

examples.source: It's also possible to cut the edges for a surface code diagonally
examples.translation: Maaari rin itong i-cut ang mga gilid ng surface code nang pahilis
examples.suggested: Maaari ring putulin nang pahilis ang mga gilid ng surface code
examples.why: 'itong' leaves a stray pronoun next to the real object 'ang mga gilid', which makes the sentence ungrammatical.

examples.source: They will only briefly be described here.
examples.translation: Bahagya lang itong tatalakaying dito.
examples.suggested: Bahagya lang itong tatalakayin dito.
examples.why: Typo: 'tatalakaying' should be 'tatalakayin'.

examples.source: Color codes are so-named because one of the required conditions on the graphs that define them
examples.translation: Ang mga color code ay nagngangalang ganito dahil isa sa mga kinakailangang kondisyon sa mga graph na nagtatukoy sa kanila
examples.suggested: Tinawag na color code ang mga ito dahil isa sa mga kinakailangang kondisyon sa mga graph na nagtatakda sa kanila
examples.why: 'nagngangalang ganito' is a stiff calque of 'so-named', and 'nagtatukoy' is not a standard verb form.

examples.source: The 7-qubit Steane code therefore possesses geometric locality
examples.translation: Ang 7-qubit Steane code ay nagtataglay ng geometric locality
examples.suggested: Kaya nagtataglay ang 7-qubit Steane code ng geometric locality
examples.why: Leaving out 'therefore' drops the logical link between the face structure and locality. The claim itself is still correct.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last 40%. The 2^{n-1}+1 worst case, the 2^{-k+1} error bound, the 1-versus-n advantage and the super-polynomial claim are all intact, so nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are wording and consistency. Entry [36] switches to English "probability", "state" and "measurement outcome", while the rest of the file uses probabilidad, estado and resulta ng pagsukat. "by the way" is calqued as "sa pamamagitan ng paraan" in [25]. "kalamangan" is misspelled "kalamantang" in [3] and [107]. In [108], the past-tense "tinalakay" should be the habitual "tinatalakay".

examples.source: these values correspond to the probability of measuring the state ... when all measurement outcomes are $0$
examples.translation: ang mga value na ito ay tumutugma sa probability ng pagsukat sa state ... kapag lahat ng measurement outcome ay $0$
examples.suggested: ang mga halagang ito ay tumutugma sa probabilidad ng pagsukat sa estado ... kapag lahat ng resulta ng pagsukat ay $0$
examples.why: Everywhere else the file uses probabilidad, estado, halaga and resulta ng pagsukat. This one entry switches to English, which breaks consistency.

examples.source: Here, by the way, we're writing binary strings...
examples.translation: Dito, sa pamamagitan ng paraan, isinusulat natin...
examples.suggested: Siyanga pala, dito ay isinusulat natin...
examples.why: A word-for-word calque of the English idiom. 'sa pamamagitan ng paraan' means 'by means of a method', not 'by the way'.

examples.source: The Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm extends this advantage
examples.translation: Pinapalawig ng Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm ang kalamantang ito
examples.suggested: Pinapalawig ng Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm ang kalamangang ito
examples.why: Misspelling of kalamangan. The same typo appears again in [107].

examples.source: the recursive Fourier sampling problem is less often discussed
examples.translation: ang recursive Fourier sampling problem ay hindi gaanong madalas na tinalakay
examples.suggested: hindi gaanong madalas na tinatalakay ang recursive Fourier sampling problem
examples.why: The English describes a habitual state, which calls for the imperfective aspect (tinatalakay) rather than the perfective (tinalakay).

examples.source: which again means that the number of input strings...
examples.translation: na nangangahulugang ang bilang ng mga input string...
examples.suggested: na muli ay nangangahulugang ang bilang ng mga input string...
examples.why: Dropping 'again' removes the reminder that 'balanced' was already defined for Deutsch's problem. The loss is small.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. Terms are consistent throughout: measurement→sukat, outcome→resulta, and positive semidefinite, density matrix and channel kept in English. A few spots need an editor's pass. In [77], the closing "if and only if" is cut to "kung at kung", which leaves the biconditional garbled, although the same entry renders it correctly earlier as "kung at kung lamang". In [71], "given an arbitrary measurement" is calqued as "dahil sa" (which means "because of"). "Describes" is sometimes rendered "nagpapaliwanag" (explains) in [26], [70] and [71], while the rest of the file uses "naglalarawan/inilarawan". In [73], "represent" became "ikinakategorya" (categorize) and "no matter what state" became "gaano man" (however much). There are also a few calques, such as "katotohanan na natutupad" for "indeed satisfied" in [94] and [102], and the typo "Ilililmita" in [6].

examples.source: The channel $\Phi$ therefore satisfies our assumption — that $\mathsf{Y}$ is classical — if and only if
examples.translation: ...na ang $\mathsf{Y}$ ay klasikal — kung at kung
examples.suggested: ...na ang $\mathsf{Y}$ ay klasikal — kung at kung lamang
examples.why: The 'only if' half of the biconditional is dropped, so the phrase is truncated. It is clearly a slip because the same entry uses 'kung at kung lamang' correctly a few lines earlier.

examples.source: Conversely, given an arbitrary measurement as a collection of matrices, there's always a valid channel ... that describes the given measurement
examples.translation: Sa kabaligtaran, dahil sa isang arbitrary na sukat bilang isang koleksyon ng mga matris, palaging may wastong channel ... na nagpapaliwanag ng ibinigay na sukat
examples.suggested: Sa kabaligtaran, kung may ibinigay na arbitrary na sukat bilang koleksyon ng mga matris, palaging may wastong channel ... na naglalarawan sa sukat na iyon
examples.why: 'Dahil sa' means 'because of', which is not what 'given' means here. 'Nagpapaliwanag' (explains) is also inconsistent with 'naglalarawan' (describes), the word used elsewhere in the file.

examples.source: we represent the measurement as a channel named $\Phi$ ... no matter what state we start with for $\mathsf{X}$
examples.translation: ikinakategorya natin ang sukat bilang isang channel ... gaano man ang estado na sinimulan natin
examples.suggested: kinakatawan natin ang sukat bilang isang channel ... anuman ang estadong sinimulan natin
examples.why: 'Ikinakategorya' means 'categorize', not 'represent'. 'Gaano man' means 'however much', so the natural phrase here is 'anuman'.

examples.source: are indeed satisfied
examples.translation: ay katotohanan na natutupad
examples.suggested: ay talagang natutupad
examples.why: This is a calque of 'indeed' that reads unnaturally. The same thing happens in [102] ('ay katotohanan na isang wastong channel').

editor_note: The core argument is carried over faithfully: linearity, trace-preserving/completely positive, the reset and dephasing examples on the Bell state, and the convex combinations. The problems are local. In [37], "what system this channel acts on" became "kung aling system ang kinakatawan ng channel na ito" ("which system the channel represents"), and "as we've already encountered" became "na nakaranas na tayo". In [33], "pinararami tayo ng U" makes "we" the thing being multiplied. Smaller slips: the raw English verb "ang qubit ay dephases" in [80], "linear na mapa" (geographic map) in [38], the truncated "sa sarili nitong" in [23], and the calque "kaya kailangan nating mayroon" in [10].

examples.source: when we wish to indicate explicitly what system this channel acts on
examples.translation: kapag gusto nating tukuyin nang malinaw kung aling system ang kinakatawan ng channel na ito
examples.suggested: kapag gusto nating ipakita nang malinaw kung saang system kumikilos ang channel na ito
examples.why: The translation says the channel 'represents' a system, but a channel is an operation that acts on a system. The subscript context mostly saves the meaning, but the wording should be fixed. In the same sentence, 'na nakaranas na tayo' should be 'na nakita na natin'.

examples.source: where we multiply by $U$ on the left and $U^{\dagger}$ on the right
examples.translation: kung saan pinararami tayo ng $U$ sa kaliwa
examples.suggested: kung saan pinararami natin ito ng $U$ sa kaliwa at ng $U^{\dagger}$ sa kanan
examples.why: The voice is wrong: 'pinararami tayo' means 'we are multiplied', not 'we multiply'.

examples.source: and with probability $\varepsilon$, the qubit dephases
examples.translation: at may probabilidad na $\varepsilon$, ang qubit ay dephases
examples.suggested: at may probabilidad na $\varepsilon$, nade-dephase ang qubit
examples.why: The English verb is left raw inside a Tagalog clause. A native writer would use a Tagalog-inflected loan verb here.

examples.source: gives us a linear map
examples.translation: nagbibigay sa atin ng linear na mapa
examples.suggested: nagbibigay sa atin ng linear na mapping
examples.why: 'Mapa' means a geographic map, and the rest of the file uses 'mapping' consistently.

examples.source: It's the same state regardless of how we choose to think about it, so we must have
examples.translation: kaya kailangan nating mayroon
examples.suggested: kaya dapat na totoo ang
examples.why: This is a calque of 'we must have' and reads unnaturally before an equation.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Monte Carlo X² versus X sample-scaling claim in [28] and the use-case criteria in [21] are both rendered faithfully. The problems are word choice and typos. In [55], "utterly disruptive" becomes "ganap na nakakaabala", which reads as "annoying" rather than industry-transforming. In [28], "fixed confidence level/time" becomes "naayos na", which means "repaired", where "takdang" was intended. [10] has the misspelling "kukumilos" and [64] has "Iplulag". [50] uses the personal marker "ni" for the company Daimler. [16] uses the unidiomatic "nagpapalaki nang exponentially", and [12] and [59] shift present-progressive "is exploring/harnessing" into past tense.

examples.source: When quantum computing scales to become utterly disruptive, we'll be ready
examples.translation: Kapag naging ganap na nakakaabala ang quantum computing sa pag-scale nito, handa na kami
examples.suggested: Kapag lumaki na ang quantum computing at tuluyang binago ang industriya, handa na kami
examples.why: 'nakakaabala' means bothersome or interrupting. It turns the business sense of 'disruptive' (transformative) into a negative, which is a calque.

examples.source: you can get to a fixed confidence level faster ... for fixed time
examples.translation: makakarating ka sa isang naayos na antas ng kumpiyansa ... para sa naayos na oras
examples.suggested: makakarating ka sa isang takdang antas ng kumpiyansa ... para sa takdang oras
examples.why: 'naayos' means repaired or arranged, not held constant. A reader can still recover the meaning from context, but 'takda/pirmi' is the correct word.

examples.source: how a molecule will behave
examples.translation: kung paano kukumilos ang isang molekula
examples.suggested: kung paano kikilos ang isang molekula
examples.why: 'kukumilos' is a misspelling. The correct future form of 'kumilos' is 'kikilos'.

examples.source: Daimler Mercedes-Benz, used quantum computing
examples.translation: Ginamit ni Daimler Mercedes-Benz ang quantum computing
examples.suggested: Ginamit ng Daimler Mercedes-Benz ang quantum computing
examples.why: 'ni' is the marker for personal names. A company needs 'ng', and the translation itself switches to 'ang Daimler' later in the same entry.

examples.source: IBM® is exploring industries where quantum computing is expected to show opportunity.
examples.translation: Nag-explore ang IBM® ng mga industriya ...
examples.suggested: Nag-e-explore ang IBM® ng mga industriya ...
examples.why: The past-tense aspect presents an ongoing effort as finished. [59] 'Nag-harness' does the same with 'is harnessing'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall, and the core terms stay consistent (ansatz/ansaetze, entanglement scheme, circuit depth, expectation value). A few spots need a native editor's pass. Entry [29] reads like machine translation: "hindi na-entangle sa iba sa lahat" copies "at all" word for word, and the English "either" is left inside "dapat na either na-entangle". Entry [31] drops "substantially", so it now says four repetitions are unlikely to give a better match at all, which is a stronger claim than the source makes. Entry [25] renders "advantageous" as "maabante" (advanced/forward) instead of "kapaki-pakinabang", and entry [11] has the typo "ilililmita".

examples.source: the last qubit is not entangled with the others at all ... should either be entangled with the others or removed
examples.translation: ang huling qubit ay hindi na-entangle sa iba sa lahat ... dapat na either na-entangle sa iba o inalis sa kalkulasyon
examples.suggested: ang huling qubit ay hindi talaga naka-entangle sa iba ... dapat itong i-entangle sa iba o kaya'y alisin sa kalkulasyon
examples.why: 'sa lahat' copies 'at all' word for word, and the English 'either' is left in the Tagalog sentence.

examples.source: is not likely to yield a substantially better match to the target state than two or three repetitions
examples.translation: hindi malamang na magbigay ng mas magandang pagkatugma sa target state kaysa sa dalawa o tatlong repetition
examples.suggested: malamang na hindi magbibigay ng mas makabuluhang pagkatugma sa target state kaysa sa dalawa o tatlong repetition
examples.why: Dropping 'substantially' makes the claim stronger (no improvement at all instead of no substantial improvement).

examples.source: Indeed that may be advantageous in cases where...
examples.translation: Sa katunayan, maaaring mas maabante iyon sa mga kaso kung saan...
examples.suggested: Sa katunayan, maaaring mas kapaki-pakinabang iyon sa mga kaso kung saan...
examples.why: 'maabante' means advanced/forward, not advantageous.

examples.source: Here, we will restrict our discussion to two-local circuits
examples.translation: Dito, ilililmita natin ang talakayan sa two-local circuits
examples.suggested: Dito, lilimitahan natin ang talakayan sa two-local circuits
examples.why: Typo/malformed verb 'ilililmita'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The course scope, the Qiskit patterns steps, the 6-10 hour estimate with two hours of video and reading, and the near-term claim about VQE all match the English, and the casual register holds with no po/opo. One polish item: entry [3] mixes languages in a single list, "mga problema sa kemikal, biochemical, o biophysical". It translates only the first adjective, and the same entry keeps "chemistry" in English. A native editor would make these consistent, either "kemikal, biokemikal, o biopisikal" or keep all three in English.

examples.source: applying quantum computing to chemical, biochemical, or biophysical problems
examples.translation: pag-apply ng quantum computing sa mga problema sa kemikal, biochemical, o biophysical
examples.suggested: pag-apply ng quantum computing sa mga problemang kemikal, biokemikal, o biopisikal
examples.why: This one list puts a Tagalog adjective next to two English ones, and the same entry keeps 'chemistry' in English. It reads as uneven, but the meaning is intact.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the VQE vs. SQD division of labour, the 70% badge threshold and the quiz-attempt limit all survive intact. There are a few wording slips. In [7], "our matrix of interest" became "aming matris na pinagsasabikan", which means a matrix we long for or are eager about. That is the wrong sense of "interest", and exclusive "aming" is odd for teaching prose. In [17], "problema ng interes" is a calque, and in [6] the perfective "lumagpas" turns an ongoing condition into a past event.

examples.source: suitable subspaces in which to project our matrix of interest
examples.translation: mga angkop na subspace kung saan ipo-project ang aming matris na pinagsasabikan
examples.suggested: mga angkop na subspace kung saan ipo-project ang matris na pinag-aaralan natin
examples.why: 'Pinagsasabikan' means yearned for or eagerly awaited, not 'the matrix under study'. Exclusive 'aming' also shuts the learner out.

examples.source: Adjust an example problem to their own problem of interest.
examples.translation: I-adjust ang isang halimbawang problema para sa sariling problema ng interes.
examples.suggested: Iangkop ang isang halimbawang problema sa sarili nilang problemang pinag-aaralan.
examples.why: 'Problema ng interes' is a word-for-word calque of 'problem of interest' and does not sound native.

examples.source: But there are still problems that exceed the limits of exact classical diagonalization algorithms.
examples.translation: Ngunit mayroon pa ring mga problema na lumagpas sa mga hangganan ...
examples.suggested: Ngunit mayroon pa ring mga problemang lumalagpas sa mga hangganan ...
examples.why: The perfective 'lumagpas' describes a finished past event. The English means an ongoing condition, so the imperfective 'lumalagpas' is needed.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The QUBO objectives, the qubit count na*nt*nq = 56, the circuit count (num_generations + 1) * population_size and the note about multiple_passmanager being temporarily disabled all come through intact, and nothing would mislead a learner. There are a few wording slips. 'consistent formatting' became 'tuluy-tuloy na formatting' (continuous), and [34] 'Nagsisimula nito' is ungrammatical. 'our paper' was calqued as 'aming papel', which reads as the physical material. The register also drifts: 'ninyo/inyong' in [23]/[24], 'iyong' plus the formal 'Mangyaring' in [43], and 'umuusbong' ('emerging') for 'evolving' in [7] is a little off.

examples.source: with consistent formatting across all assets
examples.translation: na may tuluy-tuloy na formatting sa lahat ng assets
examples.suggested: na may pare-parehong formatting sa lahat ng assets
examples.why: 'tuluy-tuloy' means continuous/uninterrupted, not uniform. The intended sense is 'pare-pareho'.

examples.source: This initiates the dynamic portfolio optimization process
examples.translation: Nagsisimula nito ang dynamic portfolio optimization process
examples.suggested: Sinisimulan nito ang dynamic portfolio optimization process
examples.why: This mixes the actor-focus verb with 'nito', which is ungrammatical. It needs the object-focus form 'Sinisimulan'.

examples.source: see [our paper](...)
examples.translation: tingnan ang [aming papel](...)
examples.suggested: tingnan ang [aming paper](...) / [aming artikulo](...)
examples.why: Calque: 'papel' reads as the physical paper. Other entries keep 'manuscript' for the same reference.

examples.source: Please take a minute ... Your insights
examples.translation: Mangyaring maglaan ng isang minuto ... Ang iyong mga pananaw
examples.suggested: Maglaan ka ng isang minuto ... Ang mga pananaw mo
examples.why: 'Mangyaring' is formal, and the file mixes 'iyong' here with 'ninyo/inyong' in [23]/[24]. The address register is inconsistent against the casual convention.

examples.source: accounts for the evolving nature of assets
examples.translation: nag-account para sa umuusbong na kalikasan ng mga assets
examples.suggested: isinasaalang-alang ang nagbabagong katangian ng mga assets
examples.why: 'umuusbong' means emerging/sprouting rather than changing over time, and 'nag-account para sa' is a calque.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and would not mislead a learner, but a native editor would change three phrases. In [19], "tumagal ng ilang oras" most naturally reads as "take several hours", which is stronger than "may take some time"; "ilang sandali" or "matagal-tagal" matches the English better. In [23], "mga pangunahing quantum" drops the noun for "basics" and reads as broken; it should be "mga batayan ng quantum". In [2], "magkakaugnay na qubit" (the plural form, "interconnected") is a loose rendering of "entangled"; "dalawang entangled na qubit" or "magkaugnay" would be more precise.

examples.source: Jobs on real hardware may take some time depending on queue times.
examples.translation: Ang mga job sa tunay na hardware ay maaaring tumagal ng ilang oras depende sa queue times.
examples.suggested: Ang mga job sa tunay na hardware ay maaaring tumagal nang ilang sandali depende sa queue times.
examples.why: 'ilang oras' is ambiguous and usually read as 'several hours', which overstates the vague 'some time'.

examples.source: structured learning paths from quantum basics to utility-scale computing
examples.translation: nakaayos na mga landas ng pag-aaral mula sa mga pangunahing quantum hanggang sa utility-scale computing
examples.suggested: nakaayos na mga landas ng pag-aaral mula sa mga batayan ng quantum hanggang sa utility-scale computing
examples.why: 'pangunahing' is an adjective with no noun here; the phrase reads as a broken calque of 'quantum basics'.

examples.source: (two entangled qubits)
examples.translation: (dalawang magkakaugnay na qubit)
examples.suggested: (dalawang entangled na qubit)
examples.why: 'magkakaugnay' means generically related or interconnected (and is plural-collective). It does not convey entanglement as a precise term.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the pm_2 counter-example, the caveats about max_iterations and the StarPreRouting scope limits, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are wrong words and calques. "dwarfs all three" became "nagtatalo" ("argues") instead of "tinatalo" in [71]. There are non-words: "nagrederita" in [34], "nananalunan" in [72] and "inimamapa" in [57]. "Minimizes SWAP gates" became "Pinipigilan" ("prevents/suppresses") in [15]. "Essentially" is calqued as "mahalaga(ng)" ("importantly") in [49], [57], [70] and [58], and "room for improvement" is calqued as "silid" in [45] and [54]. Intensifiers like "even shallower", "substantially deeper", "far less" and "much deeper" are dropped in [44], [71] and [72], which slightly flattens the emphasis.

examples.source: `StarPreRouting`, however, dwarfs all three by a substantial margin
examples.translation: Ang `StarPreRouting`, gayunpaman, ay nagtatalo sa lahat ng tatlong ng malaking margin
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, malayong tinatalo ng `StarPreRouting` ang tatlo
examples.why: "nagtatalo" means "argues/quarrels", not "beats". The context saves the meaning, but a reader stumbles on it.

examples.source: SABRE minimizes SWAP gates and reduces circuit depth
examples.translation: Pinipigilan ng SABRE ang mga SWAP gate at binabawasan ang lalim ng circuit
examples.suggested: Pinapaliit ng SABRE ang bilang ng mga SWAP gate at binabawasan ang lalim ng circuit
examples.why: "Pinipigilan" ("prevents/suppresses") claims more than "minimizes". SABRE still inserts SWAPs, it just inserts as few as it can.

examples.source: Calling `.draw()` on a stage renders its passes as a graph
examples.translation: Ang pagtatawag ng `.draw()` sa isang yugto ay nagrederita ng mga pass nito bilang isang graph
examples.suggested: Kapag tinawag ang `.draw()` sa isang yugto, ire-render nito ang mga pass bilang graph
examples.why: "nagrederita" is not a Tagalog word. It looks like a garbled rendering of "nagre-render".

examples.source: since the rewrite is essentially free compared to SABRE's stochastic search
examples.translation: dahil ang rewrite ay mahalagang libre kumpara sa stochastic na paghahanap ng SABRE
examples.suggested: dahil halos walang gastos ang rewrite kumpara sa stochastic na paghahanap ng SABRE
examples.why: "mahalaga" means "important". Calquing "essentially" this way happens in several entries and reads oddly.

examples.source: the structure-aware approach wins decisively because the circuit accumulates far less decoherence
examples.translation: ang structure-aware na pamamaraan ay mapagpasyang nananalunan dahil ang circuit ay nag-iipon ng mas kaunting decoherence
examples.suggested: tiyak na nananalo ang structure-aware na pamamaraan dahil mas lubhang kaunti ang decoherence na naiipon ng circuit
examples.why: "nananalunan" is not a word, and dropping "far" weakens the point about how big the gap is.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The technical passages are faithful: the LSb-0 bit ordering in [50], Sampler vs Estimator in [54]/[64], and the ISA/depth optimization in [60]. A native editor would still change a few things. [4] says the tutorial "ay bahagi ng nilalaman mula sa" IBM docs (is part of IBM's content) when the English says it partially draws on that content. [66] renders "specific to your problem" as the ambiguous "tiyak sa iyong problema", and "Inumberan ng Qiskit" in [50] is a stiff calque. The formal "Mangyaring" in [5]/[13] breaks the casual register. Note: I could not read the oversized entries [55]/[56] (lines 214-223, presumably embedded image data) with the file reader, so they were not reviewed.

examples.source: This tutorial partially involves content from [IBM Quantum Documentation: Hello World]
examples.translation: Ang tutorial na ito ay bahagi ng nilalaman mula sa [IBM Quantum Documentation: Hello World]
examples.suggested: Bahagyang gumagamit ang tutorial na ito ng nilalaman mula sa [IBM Quantum Documentation: Hello World]
examples.why: The translation says the tutorial is part of IBM's content instead of partially drawing on it. It is a small change in attribution, not a technical error.

examples.source: In general, this step is specific to your problem.
examples.translation: Sa pangkalahatan, ang hakbang na ito ay tiyak sa iyong problema.
examples.suggested: Sa pangkalahatan, nakadepende ang hakbang na ito sa partikular mong problema.
examples.why: 'tiyak' mostly reads as 'certain/sure', so the sentence is ambiguous. 'nagsasangkot ng postprocessing' earlier in the same entry is also a calque.

examples.source: Qiskit numbers the bits in a string from right to left.
examples.translation: Inumberan ng Qiskit ang bits sa isang string mula kanan papuntang kaliwa.
examples.suggested: Binibilang ng Qiskit ang bits sa isang string mula kanan pakaliwa.
examples.why: 'Inumberan' is past-tense and awkward for a general rule. A native writer would use present-tense 'binibilang' or 'nilalagyan ng numero'.

examples.source: please refer to this guide
examples.translation: mangyaring tingnan ang guide na ito
examples.suggested: tingnan mo ang guide na ito
examples.why: 'Mangyaring' is formal and clashes with the casual register used everywhere else. It also appears in [5].
